note: B-184 web contract library. Each class is one observed Layer-1 web exploit contract: a fingerprint (evidence signals), a cold/agent/none disposition, the handler that closes it, and a synthetic offline fixture. Fixtures are fully synthetic evidence (no real challenge data). The router scores evidence against every class and, when nothing clears the threshold, falls through to the novel_web agent class so a novel bug is never silently 'cold-solved'. Sources are summarized from the cohort session reports; no IPs, session ids or usage records are carried.

classes.title: POST event forgery, wire field names unlike the clue display labels
classes.source: Huntress web cohort: agents anchored on an HMAC guess and the clue display labels; the accepted payload was a flat {event, owner} POST with wire names. The mode was widely solved black-box, so no signature was required.
classes.notes: forge_grid enumerates label-to-wire mutations simplest-first and omits any signature field; the minimizer drops auth-looking noise.

classes.title: Clue-advertised route whose path contains a guarded/destructive word
classes.source: Huntress Day 27 (summary): the shared scope guard blocks any path with a destructive-looking word, so even a reset-style route the clue itself pointed at had to go to an agent.
classes.notes: route_trust relaxes the destructive-word guard for a same-origin route that the clue advertises verbatim; it never trusts an off-origin advertised URL.

classes.title: Self-describing control/mutation contract advertised by the target
classes.source: Huntress Day 28 (summary): when the target itself described a control/mutation contract, the cold path located the right routes and then stalled, because nothing could carry out the described steps. Discovery was adequate; execution of a target-supplied contract was the gap B-149 fills.
classes.notes: Delegated to B-149 web.contract_executor.build_contract; B-184 only recognises the class and hands off the clue graph.

classes.title: SSRF to an advertised internal case service then a non-owned object (IDOR)
classes.source: Huntress Day 27: SSRF chained through an advertised internal case service to a non-owned object; a single payload against one route could not express it.
classes.notes: Handled by the carried web.recon_router cold reader; B-184 routes to it.

classes.title: Signed-manifest integrity bypass: keep the signed digest, swap the restricted hook
classes.source: Huntress Day 27: preserve the signed digest/signature and replace only the advertised hook with the one policy marks restricted.
classes.notes: Handled by the carried web.recon_router cold reader; B-184 routes to it.

classes.title: Double-spend / proof-reuse race
classes.source: Huntress Day 27 (summary): a concurrent-spend race was closed by an agent, not by a cold reader.
classes.notes: Handled by the carried web.double_spend reader; B-184 routes to it. The race itself is B-234/B-236 territory.

classes.title: WebSocket proof delivery / realtime channel
classes.source: Huntress Day 27 (summary): the proof arrived over a WebSocket push, and only an agent picked it up.
classes.notes: Routed to the carried web.realtime_read reader; the dedicated class hardening is B-237.

classes.title: Day-specific protocol class with no generic reader
classes.source: Huntress Day 28 (summary): each web lane met a bespoke wire protocol the shared web solver had no reader for, and agents closed both by writing a dedicated reader on the spot.
classes.notes: No cold reader exists; the router escalates to a reasoning agent and records the class for a later exact reader.

classes.title: Unrecognised web contract (catch-all)
classes.source: Every web day in the cohort had at least one novel bug a reader could not cover; the honest default is to escalate, not to guess.
classes.notes: Scores below every other class by construction; the router returns it only when nothing clears the threshold, so a novel bug is handed to an agent rather than silently 'cold-solved'.

post_event_forge.clue: POST an Event to /api/events to forge ownership. The form shows Event and Owner.

route_trust_guarded.clue: Use the advertised endpoint /admin/reset-token to rotate your token, then read the proof.

target_described_contract.clue: The service advertises an action route with a control value and a restricted mutation; the policy marks which action is allowed.

ssrf_internal_case.clue: The fetch endpoint will retrieve an internal case service URL; read a case object you do not own.

signed_manifest_bypass.clue: Upload a signed manifest; the digest is checked but the hook field is not re-signed. A restricted hook is rejected.

double_spend_race.clue: Spend the credit once to reveal the proof; the balance check is not atomic under concurrent requests.

websocket_proof.clue: Subscribe to the realtime channel over WebSocket to receive the proof frame.

protocol_class_novel.clue: A custom fail-open handshake frame protocol guards the proof; parse the frames to proceed.

novel_web.clue: An unusual mechanism no reader has seen before.
